citacoes.trecho: We evaluated four major usage modes: hyperparameter optimization for decoding, zero- and few-shot prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and iterative feedback through compiler-based repair.
Specifically, in this work, we target translations between serial code, CUDA, and OpenMP.

Our findings reveal that while off-the-shelf models struggle under the default settings (e.g., GPT-4o-mini achieves only 46% compilation and 15% functional correctness), our UniPar methodology – combining fine-tuning, hyperparameter tuning, and compiler-guided repair – improves performance by up to 2X (69% compilation and 33% correctness).

The results reveal that although few-shot prompting is ineffective for this problem, both task-specific fine-tuning and agentic framework with compiler feedback deliver considerable improvement to the performance of LLMs, by up to 2X (69% compilation and 33% correctness).
System: You are an HPC expert specializing in translating between parallel programming APIs.
Each n-shot involved appending n additional examples for the same source–target language pair from the PARATRANS train set.
The results reveal that both models exhibit minimal sensitivity to the addition of few-shot examples.

While the exact cause of the poor LLM performance with the few-shot prompting would warrant further investigation, specific examples reveal that even on samples similar or identical to the one-shot prompt, LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct still introduces subtle but critical syntactic errors.

We suspect this results from a combination of context dilution with longer prompts and the nature of few-shot prompting, which is most effective at guiding answers’ high-level structure and less effective at capturing fine-grained details within that structure.
Compilation Agent: Attempts to compile the generated code. If the compilation fails, it extracts the error message and formulates a compilation repair prompt for its model.
Execution Agent: Executes the code that passes compilation. If output verification fails, it produces an output-repair prompt containing the observed behavior and invokes its model for a correction.
Both the Compilation and Execution agents used 3 rounds with GPT-4o-mini as their underlying LLM.
In general, incorporating compiler and output verifier feedback significantly improves overall performance in terms of compilation and validation rate.

This suggests that reduced randomness in the token selection process improves syntactic validity, especially when generating larger kernel codes, as supported by the findings in previous work [56], [57].
Prior studies have shown that LLM performance may degrade when processing long or unbalanced inputs, as the context window becomes saturated or loses focus [45].
In places where the code compiled successfully before the replacement but failed after the replacement, we used 3 attempts with GPT-4o-mini to repair the compilation error.
Note, three of the benchmark kernels did not pass validation and were therefore removed from subsequent experiments.

Although we checked the syntax and the functional correctness of the translated code, we did not check its runtime performance or scalability – factors that are typically important for an HPC application – nor did we ask LLMs to optimize them.
Furthermore, we have reserved an in-depth ablation study along with an evaluation of various design choices for the future.
Each component contributes independently to compilation and validation success, with their effects compounding when combined.
Compilation rates for the models across translation directions, broken down by initial generation and up to two rounds of agent-guided repair.
This feedback-driven loop continues for up to three rounds.
